newsitem.title: UK: Uruguay expected to launch global bond next week.
newsitem.headline: Uruguay expected to launch global bond next week.

text.p: Uruguay is expected to launch a $300 million 30-year global bond late next week, bankers said on Friday.
Market talk is that the bond will be priced to yield between 125-140 basis points over the 30-year U.S. Treasury note.
"It is their first bond with their new investment grade ratings," a banker said.
This week, Moody's Investors Service rated Uruguay global bonds Baa3.
The rating agency said that the combination of privatization, deregulation and reform of the social security system in Uruguay had proved successful in other developing countries such as Argentina.
Uruguay's debt and debt service burden has been reduced and the public finances stabilized, Moody's said.
Standard and Poor's upgraded Uruguay to BBB- in June. S&P said the ratings reflected, among other things, structural reforms to the public sector.
ING Barings is sole lead manager of the transaction.
The roadshow visited the U.S. and ended in New York on Tuesday, hit London today and will move to Asia next week.
"It may be launched Wednesday or Thursday next week," a banker said.
